To accommodate price reference effect, we extend the discrete choice demand model following the formulation of Kőszegi and Rabin (2006) and Gentry and Pesendorfer (2018). In addition to standard consumption utility, consumers experience gain-loss utility driven by differences between prices they rationally expect and prices they actually pay. To allow comparison across books, we model the reference price as the average discount that the consumer rationally expect for the book. Next, we analyze the equilibrium pricing decisions of the retailer facing the demand function with price reference effect.
